changes.change: An error given directly is the result before any error a reference or an array holds: tally reads the direct arguments first, in argument order, then the references and arrays in argument order. The pinned function returns the first error in argument order across all arguments.
changes.reason: Excel's capture of the dc-fwpz oracle workbook: =AND(B2,#DIV/0!) with #N/A in B2 is #DIV/0!, =AND({TRUE,#N/A},#DIV/0!) is #DIV/0!, =AND(B2,"x",#DIV/0!) is #DIV/0!, while =AND({TRUE,#DIV/0!},B2) is #DIV/0! and =AND(B2,{TRUE,#DIV/0!}) is #N/A (rows D33 to D38 of sheet logical_functions, matched in dc_fwpz__excel_comparison).

changes.change: An omitted argument and a blank cell's value given directly (the empty value, which IFNA and IFERROR return for a blank cell) are each read as a FALSE that counts as a logical; a callable (directly or held in an array), a number that is no worksheet value (NaN, an infinity or a subnormal, directly or held) and an array or a reference held inside an array are refused as FunctionFault::NotImplemented naming the argument. The pinned function leaves these to the quarantined adapters, which were not read.
changes.reason: Excel's capture: =AND(TRUE,) and =AND(,) are FALSE (rows D15 and D16), and with A7 blank =AND(TRUE,IFNA(A7,0)), =AND(IFNA(A7,0)) and =AND(TRUE,IFERROR(A7,FALSE)) are FALSE (rows D105 to D107; each inner call runs through calc_func::invoke and gives the empty value, which reaches AND directly, as on the calc-fml route, where IFNA and IFERROR take values). A non-finite number is no worksheet value (coerce::operand refuses it for every kernel). The refusals are asserted through the call interface in dc_fwpz__logical_functions, and no oracle row measures them; the subnormal number, the callable and the array or reference held inside an array are listed under not_ported with the beads that own them.

changes.change: A call outside the arity ends in FunctionFault::ArityMismatch before any argument is asked for (calc_func::invoke); AndEvalError and map_and_error_to_ws, which gave #VALUE!, are not ported.
changes.reason: Excel does not accept such a formula, so no worksheet value exists for it; the call interface reports it as a fault, as for every catalogue entry since cfunc-m1.1.

items: FunctionMeta's determinism, volatility, host-interaction, thread-safety, coercion-lift, kernel-signature and FEC-dependency classes of AND, OR, XOR, TRUE and FALSE
not_ported.basis: FunctionMeta: cfunc-m3.22 (Declare numerical sensitivity and generate backend routing) and cfunc-m3.25 (Audit complete catalogue migration and generated outputs); the other hits (cfml-m2.4, cfunc-m1.1, cfunc-m1.2, cfunc-m7.2, onecalc-m6.1) cite it for lazy forms, the first catalogue, coercion, tolerances and function exploration.

items: NOT over an array argument, which Excel lifts over its elements in a dynamic-array formula and reduces to its first element in a legacy one (=NOT(@{TRUE,FALSE}))
not_ported.basis: array evaluation and legacy array: cfml-m3.4 (Preserve array evaluation and legacy array contexts); the other hits of legacy array (cdoc-m3.3, infra-m3.2) encode or prove formulas, and array lifting and lift hit no bead that evaluates arrays.

items: NOT of text that holds a digit (=NOT("1") is #VALUE! in Excel), which coerce::logical refuses as not modelled
not_ported.basis: locale and number-text: cfml-m2.6 (Own number-format parsing and numeric text policy), whose behaviour the refused row names as its owner, as cfunc-m1.2's row IF("1",1,2) does; dc-e00t (closed) changed coerce.rs's digit-text rule and leaves text that can be a number, such as "1", refused.

items: XOR written in its package form _xlfn.XOR when a workbook is saved
not_ported.basis: _xlfn: dc-552j (Write formula prefixes and newer error values the way Excel saves them); dc-besk resolves the prefix on load and dc-xrxb handles a file's unprefixed spelling.

items: A callable (a LAMBDA, whose worksheet-visible core is #CALC!) given to AND, OR, XOR or NOT, directly or held in an array, which the kernels refuse as not modelled
not_ported.basis: callable and LAMBDA: cfml-m2.3 (Compile LET LAMBDA closures and invocation), under which dc-ibp2 refuses a callable value of IFERROR and IFNA; the other hits port callable array helpers (cfunc-m3.17), arrays (cfml-m3.4), names (cfml-m3.1), UDFs (cfml-m4.3, cfunc-m4.1), the value model (cfunc-m0.1), editing and display (chost-m3.3, dnacalc-m2.6, dnacalc-m3.1, onecalc-m2.1, onecalc-m8.1), persistence and capture matrices (infra-m2.1, infra-m3.3, infra-m7.2, cdoc-m3.1) or other work (cfml-m2.4, cfml-m2.5, cfunc-m7.2, dc-0oyu, dc-2mlz, dc-4r8u, dc-8abf, dc-lgqh).

items: A subnormal number given to AND, OR, XOR or NOT, directly or held in an array, which coerce::operand refuses as not modelled
not_ported.basis: subnormal: cfunc-m3.23 (Implement the deterministic portable Fast backend), which coerce.rs names as the owner of subnormal numbers; dc-q9rb gives a number's text and cdoc-m0.1 defines authored operations.

items: An array or a reference held inside an array given to AND, OR or XOR, which the kernels refuse as not modelled
not_ported.basis: array evaluation: cfml-m3.4 (Preserve array evaluation and legacy array contexts), the bead the round-1 search found for arrays; no oracle row measures an array that holds an array or a reference.
